My 5 mu is split the same way every year — wheat in winter, maize in summer. I've been doing this for 25 years on this same ground, so I don't change much. What worked last year I do again. The soil here is decent loam, and with the well I can water when I need to.

For wheat, I sow in early October. I use improved seed from the dealer in town — Jimai 22 or something similar. My neighbors all use it and get around 450-500 kg/mu. I buy 50 kg of compound 15-15-15 per mu and spread it before ploughing — that gives me 7.5 kg each of N, P, K in the ground. Then at jointing in spring I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu, which is another 9-10 kg of nitrogen. So my wheat gets around 17 kg N, 7.5 kg P, 7.5 kg K per mu. I'd rather put a bit extra than come up short — a bad wheat harvest means no money for maize inputs. I water 4 times: once before winter to hold moisture, then at jointing, heading, and grain filling. For spray I do it twice — once for aphids and once for rust if I see it. I plough before sowing because stubble management matters.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — no-till direct seeding saves me time and the seed goes in well. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whichever the dealer has. Base fertilizer is 40 kg compound 15-15-15 per mu at sowing (6 kg each of N, P, K), then at the 6-leaf stage I side-dress 25 kg urea (about 11-12 kg N). Total N around 17-18 kg/mu. Maize needs the nitrogen more than wheat does, I've learned that. I water 2 times if the summer rain is okay, 3 if it's dry. Spray twice — once for armyworm and once for borer. My maize usually hits 550 kg/mu, sometimes 600 in a good year.

I spend roughly the same on fertilizer each season and that's what I've budgeted. With my wife working off-farm part of the year, the farm income mostly covers our food and the kids' expenses, so I can't afford to experiment with big changes.
